Hul-az-Krakazol (I20)

Region (English scoring-table region): Serpentspine.

One-line identity: Return the Amethyst Dwarves to their lost home, and turn brewing, berserker fury, and hunting powerful foes into a way of life for an entire country.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Very long (81 directly defined missions) | Mission-tree update: Based on local v1.37.5.0; the 2022 dev diary represents its design at that time only | Uniqueness: Very high | How boxed-in it feels: Medium-high | Early pressure: High | Expansion: High

Identity and history

Hul-az-Krakazol (I20) is the ancestral hold of the Amethyst Dwarves in the Tree of Stone; it is not a living country selectable on the 1444 map. The English offline Wiki describes it as a home of master brewers, joyous carousers, and berserkers: Serpentbloom and other plants were brewed into alcohol exported throughout the dwarven empire, while special battle-brews emboldened soldiers. Exchanging a “Welcome Ale” was also a diplomatic custom; alcohol was both a commodity and a marker of identity and honour.

The brewers did not merely pass their time in taverns. Ancient Hul-az-Krakazol took part in the wars of the Jade Empire and formed mutual-defence arrangements with neighbouring holds, but later paid a heavy price when the routes failed. The Wiki dates the final fall to year 88: under siege, King Otik IV organised his people's evacuation to Rahen and stayed behind to fight; the keys to the gates were lost in the confusion. The Amethyst Dwarves who remained on the surface preserved their brewing craft but lost their home. This Wiki history connects with the current mission narrative of finding the key and reopening the tavern, but its dates belong to worldbuilding material rather than a starting event in the game.

National story and campaign arc

The player is the restorer. The Axebellow Cartel (H98) is the official-development-diary-named narrative predecessor; the current script places it around 1460, emerging from the Rajnadhaga area, and it is not a 1444 starting country. More importantly, the decision that forms Hul-az-Krakazol is not limited to H98: any qualifying dwarven adventurer company can own and core the old hold and take this route. Thus “H98 → I20” is the recommended story entrance, not the only valid chain.

After returning underground, the first great task is not conquering an empire but opening the gates, repairing the tavern, and finding ale. The Amethyst Dwarves put Serpentbloom, fungi, metals, minerals, and even magic into their brewing experiments and restore the ancient brewery Strâmolgiv. At the same time, the ruler is expected to seek worthy opponents according to the Slayers’ tradition, clear the underground passages, and treat the Command as the ultimate foe. The later missions extend into Raheni trade, land and temples, expeditions, and a fantastical endgame for potent spirits. These are mission-driven futures pursued by the player, not events that had already occurred in 1444.

Mechanics that actually define the experience

  1. Brewing and drinking are a national loop: unique decisions open the brewing menu; recipes, ingredients, and drinking states affect mission progress and the ruler. This is not a simple alcohol modifier, but a system that feeds back into campaign pacing.
  2. Slayer challenges: missions and decisions create a separate loop of seeking powerful enemies and completing hunts. Amethyst culture’s ideal of a “glorious death” can require the ruler to prove personal valour, making this restoration story rougher and more adventurous than a typical dwarven reconquest.
  3. Brewing science and artificery: ancient devices, mineral recipes, the university, and magical research push the brewery toward something like a laboratory. Many construction goals are not merely province development; they prepare the next experiment and the next drink.
  4. Underground and surface tracks: underground, you reclaim holds and passages; on the surface, you trade with Raheni states, buy land, contest resources, and may provoke resistance and war. Trade does not replace conquest; the two remain entangled.
  5. A long branching endgame: 81 directly defined missions connect brewing, hunting, the conflict with the Command, and later fantastical expeditions. The late question of whether ale can still give life meaning is a story theme, not an inevitable historical fact.

How a campaign unfolds

If you follow the H98 narrative route, begin as an Amethyst Dwarf adventurer company on the surface and survive the early situation before reaching the old hold. The predecessor appears around 1460 and must seize a specific hold, so this route has more preparation costs than a 1444 starting country; another eligible dwarven adventurer company can also form I20. Once formed, stabilise Hul-az-Krakazol and its underground passages, restore ingredient supplies and the drinking loop, then invest resources in hunting and military expansion.

The midgame is about repeatedly testing recipes and advancing the ancient brewing machinery while deciding how to handle Raheni neighbours and the Command. Powerful enemies give the Slayers a stage, but they also force serious attention to manpower, supplies, and diplomacy. The late-game objective is much larger than a single tavern: brewing and trade lead into underground wars, cross-regional operations, and an absurdly grand myth of potent spirits. If you only want to quietly develop a dwarven hold, this route will keep pulling you into war.

Formation and endgame

The I20 formation decision requires a dwarven adventurer company to control and own the old Hul-az-Krakazol hold, meet administrative-technology and city requirements, and satisfy the special Dwarovar formation conditions. Formation switches to I20’s dedicated missions. H98 is especially faithful to the official story, but is not an exclusive prerequisite. This encyclopedia gives I20 its own entry and does not misclassify H98 as another completed mission tree.

The later missions may push conquest, ale-god fantasy, and reflection on the meaning of existence to extremes. This describes the direction of a playable route; “rivers of ale” and miracles are not fixed historical facts.

Personality, values, and recommendations

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 82/100 | Autocracy 65/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 45/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 72/100) | Pluralism 20/100.

The v2.1 values score is Evil (30/100), with a Deteriorating trajectory. Restoration, brewing, and trade are not negative evidence by themselves; the decisive deductions come from exterminatory wording targeting goblins and hobgoblins in the current mission text, followed by forced territorial seizure. The same standard is applied to sapient peoples throughout the matcher; widespread prejudice in the setting does not cancel extermination.

Recommended for players who enjoy dwarven restoration, recipe experiments, hunting powerful foes, and long wars. If you dislike a late entry, underground routes, and pressure from strong neighbours, or want brewing to be a quiet tall-building activity, Hul-az-Krakazol is likely more tiring and more brutal than its name suggests.

Community experience and evidence boundary

The 2022 official development diary introduced the Axebellow predecessor and the drinking and hunting concepts; a formal release announcement from the same year included it in the Children of Ruin update. Two player materials discuss an opening alliance with Rajnadhaga, the conflict with the Command, and the route appearing around 1460. They help estimate the feel of the campaign but cannot establish current script conditions. Older posts also preserve an outdated Rubyhold-origin claim; the current appearance point is controlled by the local event/history evidence.

Identity, the Chinese name, formation conditions, and mechanics are governed by the current local Mod and Chinese localization; the English offline Wiki only supplements the ancient hold and exile history. The prior research obtained no additional readable I20 primary source through the Halann historical map, so its map extrapolations are not included here.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when this idea set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested in the idea group, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not folded into their values. A formed country's new ideas do not automatically stack with the old set. Idea descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the events had already occurred in 1444.

Hul-az-Krakazol (I20) — Amethyst Ideas

Tradition: Amethyst Traditions

Effect: Leader cost: -10%; Idea cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Master Brewers

The Amethyst Dwarves of Hul-az-Krakazol were famous for their brewing. It is said that they were the people who originally discovered the fermenting process, and created the first beers. Backed by hundreds of years of improvements, Amethyst brews are renowned for their unique flavours, quality, and potency. The quality and quantity of ale produced in the hold was of such a high standard, that the Amethyst Gem was placed in the Dwarovkron of Aul-Dwarov to honour Hul-az-Krakazol's craft, expanding their influence all across the Empire.

Effect: National unrest: -2.

Idea 2: Amethyst Hospitals

Ostensibly founded after a boisterous party got out of hand, Hul-az-Krakazol was one of the first holds to set up a permanent hospital. Called the Heilzahul, the hospital became a place for many dwarves to learn how to heal. The practice carried into wars, with field hospitals and healers up near the front lines to help heal the inevitable casualties of war.

Effect: Manpower recovery speed: +10%.

Idea 3: Green Thumbs

The best alcohol requires plants, and few holds could rival Hul-az-Krakazol's gardens and orchards. In certain caverns near the surface, the ceilings were opened up to the sky to allow the growth of plants that do not grow underground. During the early days of Aul-Dwarov, Amethyst dwarves assisted with maintaining the Serpent's Vale, taking advantage of this role to grow a variety of grains that favoured the climate of the Vale, with which they subsequently continued their experiments in beer-making and debauchery.

Effect: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Idea 4: The Valkumol

The Valkumol, or 'Welcome Ale', is an Amethyst tradition of swapping an ale or beer when having a friendly meeting, helping everyone keep a calm demeanour during negotiations. The finer the spirit, the greater the respect shown to the recipient, it being common to give the finest in all of Aul-Dwarov to the High King and many other influential visitors when visiting Hul-az-Krakazol. Failing to bring spirits to swap can be perceived as a slight, and ignoring such a tradition would often be used to begin a duel between the two parties - even if the one who forgot happened to be the High King himself.

Effect: Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 5: Berserker Battle Brew

Amethyst armies were famous for their fearlessness in battle, showing no fear even against overwhelming odds. The secret to this unnatural bravery was a special brew that soldiers drank before heading into battle, which rendered them numb to pain and doubt and fear. The secret of this battle-brew would famously spread east when, according to the legends, a lost amethyst berserker was found by a dozen Xia martial artists. Fueled by the brew and thinking himself captured, he proceeded to fight and defeat all of the warriors before coming to his senses. Impressed by this feat, these martial artists traded the Amethyst dwarf refuge and safe passage for the secret of his spirits, and with this knowledge would go on to found a new branch of martial arts focused on utilising this new brew in Liuhexingzhe, where the Way of the Drunken Fist is practised to this day.

Effect: Land morale: +15%.

Idea 6: Barrel Brigades

Warfare requires many supplies, but none are as critical as water. The Amethyst Dwarf Barrel Brigades were the logistical arm of Hul-az-Krakazol's army, and were famous for their efficacy, ensuring that the front-line soldiers always had something safe to drink. By bringing alcohol around, Amethyst armies faced far less trouble with bad water supplies than other armies, ensuring more dwarves reached the battle in good health.

Effect: Army attrition: -20%.

Idea 7: Erig’s Legacy

In the dark days of Praaq Bloodscrawl's chiefdom, The master brewer Erig Darkbarrel famously refused to abandon his brewery despite an encroaching tide of goblins. A few hundred dwarves stayed with him to delay the horde's advance while the outmatched Amethyst army rallied to the east and joined forces with Grôzumdihr. A week later, the combined armies returned to find that the brewery still stood, manned by a handful of survivors and surrounded by thousands of dead goblins. While Darkbarrel himself had fallen, his kegs still stood, stocked with ale and filled with the surviving dwarves who had celebrated their victory, swearing to defend Erig's Legacy to the last. This spirit still lingers in the armies of Krakazol, and many a mug is raised to Darkbarrel both before and after battle, swearing first to fight to the death, and second to remember the fallen.

Effect: shock_damage_received: -10%.

Ambition: Amethyst Ambition

Effect: Random candidate bonus: +1.

Axebellow Cartel (H98) — Dwarven Ideas

Tradition: Dwarven Traditions

Effect: Development cost: -10%; Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 1: Solid As Stone

As a people, we dwarves are known to be as stout and sturdy as the Serpentspine Mountains we once called our home. Eons before the Greentide, we were the bulwark against which the orcs broke, and we will break them again.

Effect: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 2: Dwarven Craftsmanship

Unlike dainty elven artistry or the soulless machinations of the gnomes, dwarven craftsmanship marries form and function with the ultimate goal of durability and reliability. Dwarven crafts are made to last, and many an ancient dwarven weapon has saved - and taken - lives well after its craftsman had perished.

Effect: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Idea 3: Masters of Defense

Dwarven citadels are the envy of all nations, with the divine Balgar the Builder first introducing man to the art of fortification.

Effect: Fort defense: +20%.

Idea 4: Blackpowder Engineering

We dwarves were the first to discover the devastating power of black powder, and many of the tunnels of ancient Dwarovar were dug using it. With word spreading of the power of hand-cannons, this will be an interesting avenue of development indeed...

Effect: Military technology cost: -10%.

Idea 5: Dwarven Resilience

Our people are hardy in body, mind, and spirit- we have had to be, given the endless waves of orcs and goblins at our doorstep. Our soldiers are among the most resolute in combat - you can count on a dwarven line not to break.

Effect: shock_damage_received: -5%; fire_damage_received: -5%.

Idea 6: Strongest Ale in the World

Our hardy constitution allows us to withstand things other races cannot; this extends to food and drink. Dwarovar Dark is the most potent ale on the planet, and will outright kill most non-dwarves - not that it has stopped them from trying.

Effect: global_spy_defence: +20%; Land morale: +2.5%.

Idea 7: Master Builders

Our architects and siege engineers are widely sought after in the human and elven courts, but their influence is best felt at home, where grand forts and terrible siege engines are churned out at breakneck speeds.

Effect: Siege ability: +5%; Construction time: -5%.

Ambition: Dwarven Ambition

Effect: Domestic trade power: +10%.
